newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press March 27.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- LONRHO TO DEMERGE AFRICAN SUGAR ARM

Lonrho is planning to sell or demerge its sugar subsidiary, Swaziland-based Lonrho Sugar Corporation, this year, independently of the planned demerger of its other African interests. Nicholas Morrell, chief executive, said that it was his intention to deal with Lonrho Sugar and Lonrho Africa as separate entities. He said the director's preference is to demerge the sugar company, giving shares to Lonrho's existing investors, but admitted that Lonrho Sugar does not meet the criteria set by the Inland Revenue for a tax-exempt demerger.
-- ABBEY CHIEF JOINS CHORUS AGAINST EMU

Chief executive of Abbey National Peter Birch has joined industrialists who fear the UK is not ready to join any form of European monetary union. He said that the UK was not ready for 1999 and that union was being driven by only two politicians, Helmut Kohl of Germany and Jacques Chirac of France. Chief executive of Barclay's Bank Martin Taylor echoed his views by warning against pressing forward with monetary union without greater economic convergence.
-- TWO TOP MACKIE MEN QUIT AS LOSS HITS 430,000 STG

Peter Long, chief executive of Belfast-based textile machinery company Mackie International, and its chairman Pat Dougan, are to step down after the company slumped to a full-year loss of 430,000 stg and cancelled its dividend. The loss was blamed on a downturn in demand for linen across the world. The group saw profits last year of three million stg. Sul Sahota, who is to take over as new chief executive, said was cautious on short-term prospects.
THE TIMES
-- BRITAIN SOARS IN WORLD COMPETITIVENESS LEAGUE

According to the International Institute of Management Development, a Swiss-based think-tank which has been compiling world competitiveness lists for ten years, Britain is soaring in the world league table of economic performance, jumping ahead of Germany and only one place behind Japan. Conservative Party strategists will seize on the improvement as clear evidence of the UK's economic success in the current general election campaign.
-- BARRATT WANTS LABOUR PLEDGE

House building company Barratt has said it is concerned that an incoming Labour government might levy VAT on new house sales. Chief executive Frank Eaton said the Housebuilders Federation has sought, since January, assurances from Labour that it has no such plans, but it has received no response. A substantial blow would be dealt to the recovery of the house market if Labour were to end the zero rating of house sales.
-- INDUSTRY WANTS 800 MILLION STG LOTTERY AID

The Industrial Group, which represents 4,500 manufacturing companies, said that lottery money could be used to create more than 300,000 jobs and improve the trade balance through the creation of an investment fund for the manufacturing sector. The Group called for 800 million stg a year of lottery funds to be diverted during the next three years to establish a national Industrial Fund. David Turnbull, director-general, said the fund would be used to encourage new and existing businesses to expand and develop in sectors where the UK is weak.
THE GUARDIAN
-- PREDATORS ON THE PROWL

Andrew Regan's plan to break-up the Co-operative movement has led to City financiers attempting to seek ways to gaining control of some of Britain's biggest membership-owned firms. Interflora, the flower delivery agency, has been forced to consult members about its future after discovering a corporate predator. At least two City merchant banks are drawing up proposals to bid for either the AA or RAC, while the Wine Society could also be at risk.
-- NEXT FASHIONS FINANCIAL OFFERING

High-street and mail order fashion retailer, Next, is considering a move into financial services and has held talks with a number of potential partners. Next already offers credit and personal loans to its customers and chief executive David Jones said the group would decide later this year whether to go ahead with the plan and who would be its partner. He said any move would be with an existing bank or financial house and any financial products would be marketed under the Next brand name.
-- STEEL DEAL WIPES OUT 8,000 JOBS

The planned merger of Germany's Thyssen and Krupp could lead to the loss of 8,000 jobs, although the company insists that half the total would have gone under existing restructuring arrangements. According to Wolfgang Clement, the economics minister of the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, the bulk of job cuts will come at Krupp. It is expected that Thyssen will have a 60 per cent stake in the group venture.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- COLLAPSE OF FREEMANS SALE STUNS SEARS

N Brown, the Manchester-based mail order group, has pulled out of negotiations to buy Freemans, the home shopping business owned by Sears. Sears is to begin talks with Littlewoods, the original buyer which walked out of a deal when the group discovered Sears was in talks with another buyer. The City has begun to question whether Sears' chief executive Liam Strong could survive this latest embarrassment.
-- 50 MILLION STG RISE IN DEUTSCHE BILL FOR MGAM

Deutsche Bank has revealed that it took a 430 million stg hit on its 1996 accounts due to the Peter Young scandal at its Morgan Grenfell Asset Management arm, 50 million stg more than expected. The bank is awaiting an imminent fine, to be over one million stg, from the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation, the industry regulator. Hilmar Kopper, the bank's chairman announced annual results of a 4.6 per cent increase in 1996 pre-tax profit.
-- POUND SURGES AFTER AMERICAN RATE RISE

The first increase in US interest rates for two years has led to a surge in the pound. Investors believe the strong economy will force rates up in Britain, although probably not until the election. The pound was also helped against the German mark and the dollar by better-than-expected trade figures and a very successful auction of gilt-edged stock. Also, trade figures show little sign that the strong pound has affected the balance of payments in January. BMC "44-171-377-1742
